findings.title: A view-only all-groups grant also grants group management
findings.body: This check accepts either the `view` or `manage` scope as proof of `canManage()`. Consequently, an administrator with only an all-groups `view` permission passes `requireManage()` for operations such as creating a top-level group. Require the `manage` scope here; a read-only grant must not authorize mutations.

findings.title: Group visibility lookup uses authorization resource IDs as group IDs
findings.body: `hasPermission` treats its argument as a group ID and looks up a resource by name, but this passes the generated authorization resource ID. The following line also adds that resource ID to the returned set, which callers use as actual group IDs to constrain user searches and counts. As a result, group-member visibility grants are not represented by the correct group IDs, causing user searches, pagination, or counts to omit permitted users or return incorrect results.

findings.title: Existing realms do not receive the new Groups schema resources and scopes
findings.body: Adding `Groups` to the schema only affects realms whose admin-permissions client is initialized after this change. `init()` returns immediately when a realm already has that client, so existing realms are not given the `Groups` resource or the new group scopes. Group permission setup or evaluation after upgrading can therefore fail because those resources and scopes are missing.
